body.p: 信号词表明讲述中的逻辑关系。By friction, I mean resistance between surfaces. 中，I mean 后是定义；For example, a sliding block slows down. 中，for example 后是具体实例。
信号词只能预判下一句是哪一类信息，具体内容要听录音。However 提示后面和前面有差别，后面那句不一定更重要。so 可能引出一个局部的结果，也可能收束整段，要看它指的范围。

cards.title: 话题与定义
rows: Today I'd like to discuss the motion of pendulums.
Let's look at the swing of a hanging weight.
The question is what controls the time of each swing.
Our focus today is the length of the pendulum.
By a cycle, I mean one complete back-and-forth motion.
The period refers to the time taken for one cycle.
Frequency is defined as the number of cycles per unit of time.
When I say …, I'm talking about …
When I say length, I'm talking about the suspension point to the weight's center.
cards.note: 引入话题的表达只说明要讲什么。记定义时，对象和条件都要记下。

cards.title: 举例与对比
rows: 支持前述观点的具体情况
For example, a staircase changes the route through a building.
一个具体实例，不代表全部
For instance, a wide doorway permits several people to pass.
Take a corridor with doors at both ends.
与前述观点对应的案例
A case in point is a room divided by a movable screen.
The hall is wide. However, its exit is narrow.
The corridor is enclosed. In contrast, the courtyard is open.
Unlike a fixed wall, a screen can be moved.
另一个方面，不一定相反
The opening improves access. On the other hand, it reduces privacy.
cards.note: 记例子时连同它说明的观点一起记，记对比时两方都记。出现例子时，话题并没有变。

cards.title: 因果与总结
rows: Because the seal leaked, air entered the container.
The seal leaked. As a result, the pressure changed.
由前述原因解释的现象
Air entered the container. That's why the pressure rose.
The uneven pressure pushes the flap. This leads to an opening.
To sum up, pressure differences can drive movement.
简要的结论，与前文一致
In short, an intact seal helps maintain the difference.
讲者要保留的中心观点
The main point is that both sides of the seal matter.
从前述证据归纳的结论
So, what this shows is that a small leak can change the system.
cards.note: because 后面是原因，不是结果。判断总结要看整段，只看一个 so 不够。

body.box: Today I'd like to discuss reversible changes. By reversible, I mean that the original state can be restored under suitable conditions. Take an ice cube: it melts into water, which can freeze again. However, burning paper doesn't provide the same kind of reversal. The main point is that a change in appearance alone doesn't tell us whether the original state can be recovered.

What does the phrase introducing the ice cube signal?
1. A correction to the meaning of reversible
2. A concrete case of the defined change
3. A contrast with a change that cannot be reversed
4. A summary of both kinds of change

body.p: Take 后面是 ice cube，这是可逆变化的一个具体例子，即第二项。纸燃烧的对比由 However 引出，整段的结论由 The main point is 引出。
这段的顺序是话题、定义、举例、对比、总结。只记冰和纸两个名词，就看不出例子和定义的关系。

lines.text: Today I'd like to discuss the role of stress in a sentence. By stress, I mean giving one word greater prominence. This use of stress concerns speech, rather than physical force.

items.stem: Which function does the phrase before the meaning of stress serve?
options: Giving another example of physical force
Stating a result of speaking more loudly
Contrasting speech with physical force
Defining how a term is being used
items.why: By stress, I mean 给出术语在这里的意思，第四项概括了这种定义的作用。

lines.text: A layer of snow can reduce heat loss from the ground. For instance, soil beneath snow may stay warmer than exposed soil during cold weather.

items.stem: What kind of information does the example signal introduce?
options: A particular comparison illustrating insulation
A definition of heat loss from the ground
A reason to reject the claim about snow
A summary of every cause of soil temperature
items.why: For instance 后面比较了积雪下和裸露的土壤，具体支持 reduce heat loss，即第一项。

lines.text: A manuscript can contain corrections made at different times. However, a difference in ink color alone doesn't prove that two people wrote it. One writer may have changed pens.

items.stem: What relation is signaled before the warning about ink?
options: An example linking a correction to a second writer
A definition of a handwritten manuscript
A limitation on interpreting a visible difference
A conclusion that ink color reliably identifies different writers
items.why: However 引出 ink color alone doesn't prove 这一限制，第三项概括了转折后的内容。

lines.text: A bridge joint leaves room for small changes in length. Because metal expands when warmed, a completely rigid connection can create stress. The joint allows some movement.

items.stem: What does the causal signal introduce?
options: The result of leaving room at the joint
The reason some movement must be allowed
A contrasting account of expansion in rigid connections
A summary of the joint's construction process
items.why: Because metal expands when warmed 是接头要留出活动余地的原因，即第二项。第一项把原因说成了结果。

lines.text: Let's look at how the arrangement of a display affects comparison. By adjacency, I mean placing things next to one another. For example, two fabric samples displayed side by side make a small color difference easier to notice. In contrast, samples placed in separate rooms must be compared from memory. Because the remembered color may be imperfect, that comparison can be less reliable. The main point is that arrangement can affect what differences become apparent, even when the samples themselves haven't changed.

items.stem: Which relation connects the two display arrangements?
options: A cause in one room followed by its result in another
A definition of adjacency followed by its restatement
A general claim followed by two similar examples
Contrast between direct and remembered comparison
items.why: In contrast 把 separate rooms 和前面的 side by side 对比：一种直接看，一种凭记忆。第四项保留了对比的两方。

items.stem: What follows the definition of adjacency?
options: A specific case involving nearby fabric samples
A denial that arrangement affects comparison
A conclusion about all remembered colors
A cause of the samples physically changing
items.why: For example 后面是 two fabric samples displayed side by side，这个实例对应 placing things next to one another，即第一项。

items.stem: What is the role of the final signal phrase?
options: To introduce a separate cause of fading
To restate the definition of adjacency
To state the conclusion about arrangement
To begin another example in a separate room
items.why: The main point is 引出 arrangement can affect what differences become apparent，这是全段的结论，即第三项。

lines.text: Our focus today is feedback in a simple control system. By feedback, I mean information about the current state that is used to adjust an action. Consider a tank with a device that measures the water level. When the level falls, a controller opens an inlet. Water enters, and the level rises. As a result, the controller eventually receives information that the desired level has been reached and closes the inlet. This is a case of using a measurement to guide a response. However, a delayed measurement can cause trouble. If the controller keeps receiving old information, it may continue adding water after the tank is already full enough. The measurement isn't useful merely because it exists; it must arrive in time for the response. Unlike a timer that opens the inlet for a fixed interval, this controller responds to the measured condition of the tank. To sum up, feedback links the state of a system to an adjustment, but the timing of the information affects how well that adjustment works.

items.stem: What does the speaker signal before explaining the meaning of feedback?
options: A contrast with the water tank
A definition of the central term
A result of an overflowing inlet
A summary of the entire explanation
items.why: By feedback, I mean 引出定义，即第二项。后面的水箱是具体例子。

items.stem: What information should be expected after the contrast signal about delay?
options: Another example of adjustment reaching the desired level
The definition of a fixed interval
A general conclusion about the measurement's accuracy
A problem that limits the control process
items.why: However, a delayed measurement can cause trouble 提示控制过程有问题，后文的 old information 说明了问题在哪，即第四项。

items.stem: What relation is marked by the comparison with a timer?
options: A difference between fixed scheduling and response to a measured state
A cause linking a fixed interval to the tank's changing level
An example of two devices using the same kind of measurement
A definition of feedback based on a predetermined time interval
items.why: Unlike a timer … fixed interval 与 responds to the measured condition 对比了两种控制方式，第一项把两方都概括了。

lines.text: Let's look at how a mechanical lock distinguishes between keys. A key's profile refers to the shape that permits it to enter a particular opening. Entering the opening, however, isn't the same as operating the lock. For example, in a simple pin mechanism, the key must also lift internal parts to suitable positions. A key can enter yet fail to produce that arrangement. Because those parts remain misaligned, the central section cannot turn. This explains why two keys that look rather similar may not operate the same lock. On the other hand, copying a key's relevant shape can allow another key to work; the lock isn't recognizing the personal identity of whoever holds it. This distinction concerns a mechanical system, not every possible way of controlling access. Electronic systems may use different kinds of information. In short, a mechanical key must meet the lock's physical requirements, and the visible ability to enter is only one of those requirements. The example shows why an initial fit can be necessary without being sufficient for the complete operation.

items.stem: What does the phrase introducing the pin mechanism lead listeners to expect?
options: A conclusion comparing electronic and mechanical access
An explanation of how a copied key identifies its holder
A concrete example of an additional physical requirement
A definition of the profile needed to enter the opening
items.why: For example 引出 key must also lift internal parts，说明钥匙插进去之后还有别的条件，即第三项。

items.stem: What is introduced by the causal signal about internal parts?
options: A definition of a key's visible profile
The reason the central section cannot rotate
A summary of the requirements shared with electronic systems
A contrast between a copied key and its original
items.why: Because those parts remain misaligned 是原因，the central section cannot turn 是结果，第二项保留了这个因果方向。

items.stem: What information does the final summary signal introduce?
options: A general conclusion combining the lock's physical requirements
A new example of an electronic identification method
A revised claim that the visible profile is the decisive requirement
A detailed account of how a particular key was copied
items.why: In short 把 physical requirements 和 only one of those requirements 合在一起，第一项概括了这个总结。
